title: Chemical reactions
intro: New substances from old ones: learn the signs of a chemical reaction, word equations, burning, rusting and why mass is never lost.
description: Free KS3 Chemistry questions with answers on chemical reactions: physical and chemical changes, signs of a reaction, word equations, combustion, oxidation, conservation of mass and gas tests. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9.

subtopics.title: Conservation of mass and gas tests

questions.q: Which of these is a **chemical** change?
questions.hint: In a chemical change, a new substance is made.
questions.explain: Toasting makes new substances (the brown, crispy part). Melting, dissolving and breaking don't make new substances.

questions.q: Which of these is a **physical** change?
questions.hint: Can you easily get back what you started with?
questions.explain: Freezing water makes ice, which is still water. You can melt it back. That's a physical change.

questions.q: Which is a sign that a chemical reaction has happened?
options: Bubbles of a new gas are given off
The substance is cut into pieces
The substance is poured into a jug
questions.hint: Look for signs that something new has been made.
questions.explain: Signs of a chemical reaction include a gas being given off, a colour change, a temperature change and a new solid appearing.

questions.q: In a reaction, the starting substances are called…
questions.explain: The starting substances are reactants. The new substances made are products.

questions.q: A reaction makes the test tube feel hotter. What kind of reaction is it?
questions.hint: Exo- means “out”: energy goes out to the surroundings.
questions.explain: An exothermic reaction transfers energy to the surroundings, so they get warmer. Burning is exothermic.

questions.q: Magnesium burns in oxygen to make magnesium oxide. Which is the word equation?
questions.hint: Reactants go on the left of the arrow, products on the right.

questions.q: In “zinc + hydrochloric acid → zinc chloride + hydrogen”, which are the products?
questions.hint: Products are on the right of the arrow.
questions.explain: The products are zinc chloride and hydrogen.

questions.q: Copper carbonate is heated and breaks down into copper oxide and carbon dioxide. What type of reaction is this?
questions.hint: Thermal means heat, decomposition means breaking down.
questions.explain: One substance is broken down by heating into simpler substances: thermal decomposition.

questions.hint: It's a reaction with oxygen that gives out heat and light.
questions.explain: Burning is combustion: a fuel reacts with oxygen and transfers energy as heat and light.

questions.q: The fire triangle shows the three things a fire needs. Which list is right?
questions.hint: Take away any one and the fire goes out.
questions.explain: A fire needs fuel, heat and oxygen. A fire blanket works by cutting off the oxygen.

questions.q: When a fuel like natural gas (methane) burns completely, what two products are made?
questions.hint: The fuel contains carbon and hydrogen; each joins with oxygen.

questions.q: Iron rusts when it reacts with…
questions.hint: Iron doesn't rust in dry air or in water with no air in it.
questions.explain: Rusting needs both oxygen (from air) and water. Rust is a form of iron oxide.

questions.q: Why does painting a bike frame stop it rusting?
options: It keeps air and water away from the iron
questions.hint: What does iron need to rust?
questions.explain: Paint is a barrier that stops oxygen and water reaching the iron.

questions.q: 24 g of magnesium reacts with exactly 16 g of oxygen. What mass of magnesium oxide is made?
questions.hint: Mass is never created or destroyed in a reaction.
questions.explain: 24 + 16 = 40 g. The atoms are just rearranged.

questions.q: Wood is burned and the ash weighs much less than the wood. Where did the mass go?
options: Into gases like carbon dioxide and water vapour that escaped
questions.hint: Atoms can't vanish. What left the fire?
questions.explain: The mass went into gases that escaped into the air. If you caught all the products, the total mass would be the same as the wood plus the oxygen used.

questions.q: Which test shows a gas is **carbon dioxide**?
options: It burns with a squeaky pop
It turns blue litmus red and smells of eggs

questions.q: A lit splint is held near a test tube and you hear a squeaky pop. Which gas is it?
questions.hint: The pop is a tiny explosion.
questions.explain: Hydrogen burns with a squeaky pop.

questions.q: A glowing splint relights when put into a test tube of gas. Which gas is it?
questions.explain: Oxygen relights a glowing splint because it helps things burn.
